definitions.per_diem: Fixed daily allowance for meals and incidentals as an alternative to itemized reimbursement.
definitions.m_and_ie: Meals and Incidental Expenses component of federal per-diem rates (distinct from lodging).
definitions.tier: City classification matching TEP-004 lodging tiers.
definitions.intermediate_day: Full business travel day that is not departure or return day.

rules.source_quote: Per-diem is for trips lasting 3 or more consecutive nights; shorter trips must use itemized meal reimbursement under TEP-002.
Per-diem vs itemized must be declared at trip start and may not be changed mid-trip.
Per-diem covers meals/incidentals only; lodging (TEP-004) and ground transport (TEP-006) are actual cost separately.
Tier 4 (international) per-diem rate is set at trip approval.
Departure and return days are 75% of daily rate; intermediate days are 100%.
Per-diem does not cover alcoholic beverages (TEP-003 applies for sanctioned client entertainment).
Client entertainment meals are itemized under TEP-002 §4, not from per-diem.
Per-diem does not cover lodging or ground transportation.
Phone, internet, and business communications are not covered by per-diem.
Individual meal receipts are not required when per-diem is elected (TEP-007 §4.3), but itemized meal reimbursement is not allowed.
Employee must maintain documentation of trip duration and destination.
International destinations outside Tier 1–3: rate set at trip approval per U.S. State Department M&IE.
